name: M1 — Interactive web relay demo
releaseDecision: GO for the explicitly listed local demo workflows. NO-GO for full-design or production completion.
model: Real CLI sessions and shell/file execution. Built-in demo agents use scripted responses; Custom API agents connect to the supplied private provider.

requiredDemoFunctions.name: Account and hub selection
requiredDemoFunctions.try: Sign in as Alice, open Home demo and Work demo. Sign in as Bob in a separate browser profile: only Home demo and Home laptop are visible.

requiredDemoFunctions.name: Multiple Computers per hub
requiredDemoFunctions.try: Home demo contains Home laptop and Home workstation. Work demo has its own Work computer. Each Computer has exactly one hub.

requiredDemoFunctions.name: Agent creation and conversation
requiredDemoFunctions.try: Select a Computer, choose New agent, choose Pi, then send a message. Replies explicitly identify the scripted model.

requiredDemoFunctions.name: Actual local tool execution
requiredDemoFunctions.try: Send run demo tool. Pi executes the supplied shell command in its isolated workspace. Open proof.txt to inspect the result.

requiredDemoFunctions.name: Full browser workspace
requiredDemoFunctions.try: Use Open workspace. View Git changes, search files, read and download welcome.txt, edit and save it, upload an attachment, and search the conversation.

requiredDemoFunctions.name: Computer-owned remote queue
requiredDemoFunctions.try: Send run demo tool, then queue another prompt during its five-second tool run. Edit the queued prompt. It runs after the current turn when authorization is available.

requiredDemoFunctions.name: Private unsent drafts
requiredDemoFunctions.try: Alice and Bob can open the same Home laptop agent. Each account keeps its own unsent text.

requiredDemoFunctions.name: Invitations and inherited retention
requiredDemoFunctions.try: Alice uses Manage access to invite Bob to another computer, or remove him. Set the hub removal policy to Read-only: Bob keeps the existing transcript but cannot send or create agents. An explicit hub policy overrides the computer policy.

requiredDemoFunctions.name: Delegated workspace files
requiredDemoFunctions.try: Alice grants Bob Read files or Read and edit files in Manage access. Bob can access files only inside that Computer’s configured workspace. Removing the grant or membership removes file access.

requiredDemoFunctions.name: Owner-only deletion and launch recovery
requiredDemoFunctions.try: Delete a disposable session using the normal confirmation. Operators cannot delete. Check launch result recovers saved launch receipts without dispatching another launch; automated fault tests exercise the lost-response case.

requiredDemoFunctions.name: Duplicate and conversation settings
requiredDemoFunctions.try: Duplicate a configured agent from its sidebar card: the copy stays on its source Computer. Private launch credentials/settings must be re-entered through New session. Edit conversation name, priority and snooze; dependencies are limited to accessible agents on the same Computer.

requiredDemoFunctions.name: Resume a saved session
requiredDemoFunctions.try: Choose New session, then Start → Resume saved session. Choose the original Computer and runtime, enter its original working directory and use Find saved sessions to select a saved session, or enter its backend session ID. Re-enter private provider settings when needed. Complete runtime setup and workspace trust locally first; an already-running session should be selected instead of resumed.

requiredDemoFunctions.name: Discovery and reconnect feedback
requiredDemoFunctions.try: A fresh page shows Discovering sessions while catalogs load. An unreachable hub or Computer has an explanation, Hubs & computers and Retry discovery controls. A temporary Computer failure retains only currently authorized known sessions.

requiredDemoFunctions.name: Claude setup and early messages
requiredDemoFunctions.try: Complete Claude onboarding, workspace trust and provider/key/permissions confirmations locally on the Computer. Missing setup leaves the creation form intact with instructions. If Claude is still starting, a rejected send preserves the typed message; send it again after the native editor is ready.

noGo.reason: Delegated file grants deliberately do not authorize repository history; it can contain data outside the current approved working tree. Git access currently requires the computer owner.

noGo.reason: Upload staging uses computer-wide storage outside the delegated workspace boundary. Only the computer owner can use the current upload route.

noGo.function: Unified terminal-local and remote queue management
noGo.reason: Remote prompts use the new durable authorized queue; existing local queues remain separate. The remote queue waits for local work, but there is no single ordered queue or local UI for all remote items.
noGo.exit: Define one ordering/dispatch boundary and test simultaneous local/remote edits, revocation and restart without duplicate sends.

noGo.function: Relay import of old PID-only broker sessions
noGo.reason: A reused process ID cannot safely identify a runtime instance. Relay import rejects old PID-only IDs rather than applying old permissions to a replacement process. Existing direct sessions remain available.
noGo.exit: Continue the session in direct mode or resume it under the updated UUID-based broker; any automatic migration needs a separately verified identity proof.
noGo.owner: Computer owner for session migration; implementation agent for any automatic migration

Installed Pi across three private API protocols, Codex and Claude endpoint/key/model checks 5/5; Codex and Claude browser create/send/transcript/reload and trusted Codex resume 7/7; native HTTP/Git/media 19/19 and PTY/session 12/12. Actual Pi browser verifies tools during hub outage, files/Git/CAS/search/queue, producer-confirmed model/effort controls, real provider stream interruption, creation receipt recovery, attachment metadata and private drafts. All 23 native workspace acceptance checks pass, including delegated edit/revocation, membership loss, owner deletion authorization and hub-first read-only retention. The Docker wrapper exits 0 and cleans up its own resources.
